questions.q: Who is speaking to the crowd in the square with 'the great bull voice'?
questions.explain: 'The voice has magic in it... A lion growls in it, and thunder echoes in it over black mountains.'

questions.q: How do Dubula and Tomlinson regard John Kumalo's oratory?
choices: With 'contempt, and with envy' — a voice to move thousands 'with no brain behind it... with no courage to say it if it knew'
questions.explain: They say Tomlinson has the brains and Dubula the heart, but John Kumalo has only the voice.

questions.q: What is John Kumalo asking for in his speech?
choices: Equality, the vote and the removal of the colour bar
Only 'our share' of the wealth produced by black labour — more money from the richest industry in the world
questions.explain: 'We are not asking here for equality and the franchise... We are asking only for more money.'

questions.q: Why, according to the narrator, does John Kumalo always 'go so far and no further'?
choices: He runs out of things to say
He is afraid — he knows that truly rousing words would send him to prison, and 'There is no applause in prison'
The police stop him each time
questions.explain: 'He is corrupted by his possessions, and he fears their loss.'

questions.q: What do the two policemen say about John Kumalo?
choices: 'This man is dangerous' — 'Why don't they shoot him?'
questions.explain: The high officer later calls him 'Yellow' — dangerous, but a coward.

questions.q: How does Jarvis react to hearing John Kumalo speak?
choices: 'I don't care for that sort of thing' — he wants to move on to the Boys' Club
He wants to meet the speaker
questions.explain: John Harrison thinks, 'He's too old to face it... Just like my father. But we have to face it.'

questions.q: What is Msimangu's judgement on John Kumalo's power?
choices: That he should use it fully
'Perhaps we should thank God he is corrupt. For if he were not corrupt, he could plunge this country into bloodshed.'
That it is a gift from God to be admired
questions.explain: 'Why God should give such power is not for us to understand.'

questions.q: What happens with the mine strike in this chapter?
choices: It spreads to the whole country
It never goes beyond the mines; the worst is at Driefontein, where police drive the miners underground and three are killed
It is called off before it starts
It succeeds and wages are doubled
questions.explain: 'All is quiet, they report, all is quiet.'

questions.q: What did a clergyman urge at the Annual Synod of the Diocese of Johannesburg?
choices: That it was time to recognize the African Mine Workers' Union — and he 'prophesied a blood-bath if it were not'
That the church stay out of politics
questions.explain: A 'spokesman' replies that the miners are 'simple souls... an easy tool for unscrupulous agitators.'

choices: 'Nothing is ever quiet, except for fools.' — after images of water lapping a deserted harbour and a white ant eating hidden wood
questions.explain: The official calm hides deep, continuing decay.
